explainBack.prompt: Why did fine-tuning on the companies' private protein structures make the model score better on the held-out test, and why doesn't that mean a medicine is coming?
explainBack.response: The five companies contributed 20,167 protein–molecule structures that public datasets lack, so the model saw more real examples of how proteins and molecules fit together. When tested on examples kept out of training, it predicted more structures accurately than models trained only on public data. But that score only measures prediction quality on that test; making a medicine still requires designing a compound, testing it in labs and clinical trials, and showing patient benefit — none of which this report contains.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer should cite the private data as the training input, the held-out test as the measurement, and name the missing downstream stages (public model, peer review, tested drug, patient outcome).
explainBack.assessment: The artifact fully supports this answer: P002 gives the data-to-test chain, P003 defines the held-out test and the not-public/not-peer-reviewed limits, and P004 names the missing stages. Explain-back succeeds.

unseenTransfer.prompt: Using this article's mental model, how should a reader classify the startup's claim and what should they look for next?
unseenTransfer.response: This is a model-benchmark claim, the first of the article's three categories. The extra hospital scans plausibly improved the test score the same way pooled private protein data did, but a 94% held-out score does not show the tool helps real patients. The reader should look for whether the model is available and independently reviewed, whether a prospective clinical study exists, and whether any patient outcome (faster correct diagnosis, better recovery) is reported — before accepting 'transform pneumonia care'.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: A correct transfer applies the model/tested-intervention/patient-outcome sorting from P004 and the not-public/not-peer-reviewed caution from P003 to a domain absent from the article.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers cleanly and completely to this new medical-imaging case with no missing pieces; unseenTransfer passes on P003–P004.

artifactEvidence.excerpt: Nature reports that five drug companies used 20,167 private protein structures to fine-tune a research AI model based on OpenFold3. On a held-out test, the reported model predicted more protein–molecule structures accurately than comparable models trained on public data alone. This is a research-model comparison, not an announcement of a new drug.
